about: Labelled requirement lines for scripts/solutions.mjs. solution=false must never warn; at least 85% of solution=true must. Add a line whenever the warning is wrong in a real run.

cases.text: A customer can find the nearest branch open on Saturday.
A customer can commit to a fixed-term deposit and sees the maturity date before confirming.
A teller sees the queue of customers waiting at their branch.
A clinic receptionist sees the waiting queue in arrival order.
A patient sees a table of their last 12 blood pressure readings.
A nurse completes the discharge workflow in under 3 minutes.
A shopper buying cookies sees the allergen list before adding them to the basket.
A seller can export their orders as a spreadsheet with one column per field shown on the order page.
Running the tool with --json prints the result as JSON so scripts can read it.
The deploy command exits non-zero when any step fails.
A user can filter log lines with a regex.
Yesterday's sales appear in the finance report by 06:00 each day.
A record that fails validation is quarantined and the data owner is told the same day.
Every action on the checkout page can be completed with a keyboard alone.
A screen reader user hears the error message when a field is invalid.
Search returns results in under 300 ms at p95 for 1 million products.
A learner can resume a training module where they left off.
Customer data is migrated to the EU region before 2027-01-01 per the regulatory framework.
A customer sees the sort code and account number on the statement.
Table 3 of the return shows the totals.
A visitor at the public address always gets the latest released version of the page.
The page never collects, keeps or sends anything about the visitor, and nothing on it comes from another site.
If the public page stops working or serves an old version, the owner hears about it within a day.
A signed-in shopper can save an in-stock item to their saved list. Needs: who the shopper is.
Saving a 201st item is refused with "Your saved list is full (200 items)".
The app works on iOS, macOS and Android, and on an iPhone SE screen.
A merchant sees the order status change to Shipped within a minute of the courier scanning it.
A partner calling GET /v1/rates receives the current exchange rates.
An unauthenticated call to the API gets status 401 and no data.
A partner can register a webhook and receives an event within 5 seconds of a payment settling.
The response lists each rate with `currency` and `rate`.
Store the session token in a database.
The service writes to the orders store in Postgres.
The frontend uses react hooks to load state.
Persist the cart in browser storage.
Call the payments service over gRPC.
The handler is triggered by a Pub/Sub message.
Write events to the event bus and an SQS queue.
Add an index on customer_id.
Use a feature flag in LaunchDarkly.
The page includes a script tag pointing to the CDN.
Cache the response in memcached for 60 seconds.
Expose a new route /api/orders.
The Lambda function writes to DynamoDB.
Use the useEffect hook.
Save to the saved_items collection in Mongo.
The api returns the new rate.
Database rows are soft-deleted.
The microservice publishes to a Kafka topic.
Deployed via GitHub Actions to Vercel.
Use an ORM model SavedItem with a foreign key to User.
The conversion module, imported directly in Node with no browser, returns the same results.
The live page responds with HTTP 200 and contains `<meta name="build" content="<sha>">` whose sha equals the main commit.
The page writes no cookie, local storage or session storage.
POST /saved stores the item in the saved_items table.
